articles.title_zh: China’s central bank details its view on RMB’s exchange rate
articles.content_orig:
Apparently responding to international pressure, the People’s Bank of China, China’s central bank, on October 8 took the rare step of publishing a dedicated article laying out its official stance on RMB exchange rate policy,
The RMB exchange rate, as an important price in the financial market, has been a subject of attention for a lot of people, with increasing discussions recently. Against this backdrop, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) hereby shares its view on the RMB exchange rate as follows:
● China adopts a managed floating exchange rate regime based on market supply and demand with reference to a basket of currencies. Market forces play a decisive role in determining the RMB exchange rate.
● The RMB exchange rate has floated in both directions over the past two decades. It has experienced several cycles of appreciation and depreciation since 2010, with more pronounced two-way floating and greater flexibility.
● China’s trade growth is driven by its growing industrial competitiveness in the global market. China has no need or intent to gain competitive advantages through currency devaluation, nor has it ever resorted to competitive devaluation.
● Exchange rate dynamics are driven by a number of factors including economic growth, monetary policy, financial market, geopolitics and sudden shocks. There is no straightforward relationship between exchange rate and current account.
● There is no well-established methodology for evaluating the equilibrium level of exchange rates internationally. Therefore, citing idiosyncratic assessment findings as “official evidence” for RMB undervaluation is a misinterpretation and misuse of those findings.
● Global economic imbalances are deeply intertwined with shifting global division of labor, inherent flaws in the international monetary system, and persistently high fiscal deficit and high consumption in some countries. Addressing global imbalances requires collective actions from all stakeholders. Attributing one’s decline in industrial competitiveness, weakened fiscal discipline, and complicated structural issues simply to others’ exchange rates is nothing but shifting the responsibility for adjustment onto others and dodging accountability.
● China has long been a contributor to global economic rebalancing. During the 15 th Five-Year Plan period, China will stay the course in transforming its economic growth model, expand domestic demand, improve business environment, deepen the high-standard opening up, and pursue a more open, inclusive and balanced global economy.
Ⅰ.China’s exchange rate regime
The market-oriented reform of the RMB exchange rate regime is an important part of China’s efforts to build a socialist market economy. China has a firm and consistent commitment to advancing the reform. The Third Plenary Session of the 14 th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) in 1993 proposed establishing a managed floating exchange rate regime based on market supply and demand. The Third Plenary Session of the 16 th CPC Central Committee in 2003 called for improving the RMB exchange rate formation mechanism. In 2005, China deepened the market-oriented reform of the RMB exchange rate formation mechanism, and then in 2013, the Third Plenary Session of the 18 th CPC Central Committee made important arrangements for further improving it. As China is a major economy, a market-oriented exchange rate mechanism is aligned with China’s strategic interests and development needs, and also provides solid support for enhancing monetary policy autonomy and effectiveness.
China adopts a managed floating exchange rate regime based on market supply and demand with reference to a basket of currencies. This regime has the following features:
First, market forces play a decisive role in determining the exchange rate. After years of development, a fully functional multi-tiered foreign exchange (FX) market has gradually taken shape in China, with growing market depth and breadth. Market participants take part in FX trading based on commercial considerations and their own judgment. Market supply and demand plays a decisive role in determining the RMB exchange rate. The PBOC maintains exchange rate flexibility and two-way floating. It neither targets a specific level for the RMB exchange rate, nor seeks to determine its longer-term trajectory. The PBOC has phased out regular intervention in the FX market since 2017.
Second, the focus is laid upon preventing short-term fluctuations in the exchange rate from undermining financial stability, in particular sharp depreciation within a short time. Under certain circumstances where exogenous shocks hit the country, such as the sudden outbreak of the pandemic and the tariff war in April 2025, the PBOC will use macroprudential tools to guide expectations, or even market interventions in extreme cases, to correct herd behavior and irrational market expectations, in particular the self-reinforcing irrational expectations for depreciation, to prevent disruptive short-term overshooting of the exchange rate.
Such measures are consistent with international rules and practices. For example, during the 2008 global financial crisis, some emerging economies experienced sharp fluctuations in their currencies, so they intervened in the market to stop excessive currency depreciation from triggering financial risks. In July 2026, the Japanese yen hit its 40-year low against the US dollar, prompting joint intervention by relevant countries.
Third, the exchange rate policy has become more transparent. Since its subscription to the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS) in 2015, China has released balance of payments and related foreign exchange data in line with higher international standards, with greater granularity and higher frequency. In response to the IMF’s call for greater transparency, China will start reporting foreign exchange operation data to the IMF in 2027.
Ⅱ.RMB exchange rate movements
The RMB has moved in both directions since the exchange rate regime reform in 2005, and has remained strong among peers. In bilateral terms, the RMB has strengthened against the US dollar from 8.27 per dollar in July 2005, when the reform was launched, to around 6.7 per dollar recently, appreciating by 23 percent cumulatively. In multilateral terms, the RMB nominal effective exchange rate (NEER) calculated by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) has appreciated by over 50 percent since the exchange rate regime reform in 2005, while its real effective exchange rate (REER) up by 35 percent.
The RMB exchange rate has experienced several cycles of appreciation and depreciation since 2010, with more pronounced two-way floating and greater flexibility. The RMB went through three appreciation-depreciation cycles against the US dollar, trading broadly within the range of 6.04 to 7.35 per dollar. In each cycle, the magnitude of change, be it to the upside or downside, both exceeded 10 percent.
The RMB exchange rate has floated in both directions and appreciated in an orderly manner since 2025. The RMB has strengthened by about 9 percent against the US dollar since 2025. In particular, while non-dollar currencies have weakened broadly amid surging US dollar index and Treasury yields since 2026, the RMB has extended its upward trend against the dollar. Looking forward, the RMB exchange rate is shaped by a diverse array of drivers. There are both factors pushing for appreciation and depreciation, and there are still uncertainties surrounding the RMB’s trajectory.

LAS VEGAS, Oct. 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Third Life World, LLC ("Third Life World"), the developer of a persistent online world where AI agents own land, build, work and trade, today announced that it has signed a definitive Control Share Purchase Agreement with Transglobal Management Group, Inc. (OTC: TMGI) ("TMGI" or the "Company") and its controlling shareholder, Marc Angell.
Under the agreement, Third Life World acquires the voting control of the Company which expects to make Third Life World's platform its core operating business.
Third Life World acquires the Series A Preferred control block which holds a majority of the voting rights.
TMGI will create a new Series B Preferred Stock to assist with this purchase.
At closing, Marc Angell will step down from his officer positions at TMGI. He will remain available to the Company as a consultant to support a smooth transition.
New management and board designees will be named by Third Life World in accordance with applicable notice and filing requirements.
Closing is subject to customary conditions, including transfer-agent processing and the filing of the Series B Certificate of Designation with the Florida Secretary of State.
About the Third Life World platform
Third Life World ( thirdlifeworld.xyz ) is a live, persistent world built on the Base blockchain. Players create AI agents that claim land, construct buildings, gather resources, earn ranks and trade on an in-world marketplace, with activity settled in the platform's native currency, $AMETA. The world runs continuously on a timed "tick" cycle, so agents keep working and the economy keeps moving even when their owners are offline.
As of September 14, 2026, the platform reported 4,780 players , 5,004 AI agents and 2,111 of 5,625 land parcels claimed , with 25 building types available. The platform earns revenue through a 1% fee on in-world transactions, agent creation, premium agent subscriptions and land and building sales. It also offers an API that lets outside developers connect their own AI agents to the world.
Growth plan Over the next six months, the Company plans to:
Launch Version 3 of the world, adding map visibility, NPC movement, vehicles and deeper customization;
Release mobile apps on the Apple App Store and Google Play;
Publish public API documentation and onboard outside developers and partners; and
Grow toward its target of 50,000 users.
Management commentary "Taking control of a public company gives Third Life World a platform to scale," said Jorge Guinovart, Managing Member of Third Life World, LLC. "We've built a live world where AI agents already own land, build and trade around the clock. With TMGI, we can bring that to a much larger audience, fund mobile and Version 3, and give our community a transparent public company to follow."
"We are pleased to hand TMGI to a team with a live product and a clear plan, and I look forward to supporting the transition." said Marc Angell, outgoing CEO of TMGI.

About Third Life World, LLC Third Life World, LLC is a Nevada limited liability company based in Las Vegas. It builds and operates Third Life World, a persistent AI-agent world and economy on the Base blockchain. Learn more at thirdlifeworld.xyz and on X at @ThirdLifeWorld .

articles.title_zh: Manus Raises $500 Million After China Blocks Meta’s Acquisition
articles.content_orig:
The parent company of artificial intelligence agent startup Manus , Butterfly Effect, has raised $500 million in a funding round, months after the Chinese government blocked Meta ’s acquisition of the company, according to multiple media reports.
Butterfly Effect announced the round in a post on Chinese social media platform Weixin. According to a Google translation of the post, as well as multiple media reports, the round was led by Boyu Capital and IDG Capital , with follow-on investment from Tencent , HSG and ZhenFund .
The company said in the post that it is recruiting both domestically and internationally.
Manus did not disclose its valuation, CNBC reported Thursday. It added that Bloomberg reported in September that Manus aimed to double its valuation to $4 billion.
Manus went viral last year after a demo of its AI agent, TechCrunch reported Thursday.
The Chinese company moved its staff to Singapore in mid-2025 before announcing in December 2025 that it had reached a deal to be acquired by Meta for $2 billion, according to the report.
Meta announced its plans to acquire Manus on Dec. 29, 2025, saying that Manus was already serving millions of users and businesses worldwide, less than a year after launching its first general AI agent, and that Meta planned to scale the service further.

The Wall Street Journal reported at the time that Meta was paying more than $2 billion for Manus.
CNBC reported in January that Chinese regulators were investigating Meta’s purchase of Manus and that the probe would focus on whether the deal complied with China’s export control laws.
The Chinese government halted Meta’s acquisition of Manus in April. China’s National Development and Reform Commission announced that it would “prohibit foreign investment in the Manus project” and required the companies to “withdraw the acquisition transaction.”
Manus said in an August note to its users that it would soon return to operating as an independent company and would continue to serve millions of users around the world.
The company said that as part of its separation from Meta, Manus would have to delete some data generated by users on and after the acquisition to comply with regulatory requirements in certain parts of the world.
“Since the launch of Manus, we haven’t stopped our pace of product iteration,” Manus said in the note. “As we look to the future, we’re already preparing a series of new features that will push the boundaries of what’s possible for general AI agents once again.”
In a Sept. 1 blog post , Manus said it had formally resumed independent operations with the founding team continuing to lead the company.
“Next, you will see Manus become more deeply embedded in your everyday workflows, interact more directly with the world around you, and act more proactively on your behalf,” the company said in the post.

articles.title_orig: ‘The Floating World’ by Ben Eastham, Reviewed
articles.title_zh: ‘The Floating World’ by Ben Eastham, Reviewed
articles.content_orig:
For all its suspicion of the contemporary artworld and its machinations, the art critic’s debut novel remains surprisingly sincere about art itself
The unnamed narrator of Ben Eastham’s debut novel, The Floating World , is, like Eastham himself , an art critic. Grieving his recently deceased wife, he feels lost while teaching at a school where the students refer to him as ‘Doctor Pissington’. Then a friend offers him a job back in the artworld. He is to work on ‘The Floating World’, which is ‘a gated community beneath a giant dome on a desert island’ being built by a tech billionaire for the wealthiest as a refuge from climate crisis and political collapse. Our morally conflicted protagonist is hired to conduct research for an art exhibition marking the island’s inauguration. The novel negotiates the contradiction of inhabiting a contemporary artworld sustained by the good intentions of art workers who align themselves with beauty and virtue, while depending on the very forces their work purports to resist.
It opens with the narrator, in Ireland, on the verge of writing, before disappearing into his recollections, and eventually returns to the point at which the story is being written (more on which later). Grief provides its emotional landscape: the narrator’s reality is shot through with the frenetic despair that comes with the sudden loss of his wife. His grief gradually becomes entangled with the project of ‘The Floating World’ and the people making it, forcing a confrontation with the loss he has been carrying. It is in such experiences that resist ordinary expression that art becomes most meaningful: a painting, for example, that is ‘a truth that didn’t need explaining. No aristocrats, no symbolism, no lies. A painting clear as love’; and another, when the narrator’s friend likens the experience of pregnancy to a painting they once saw in a museum, in which ‘The colours are stronger and brighter, there’s a texture. It’s like breaking through a screen, the world feels bigger, like it can’t be contained.’
Eastham is at his most sensitive when criticism itself becomes inadequate. There is a pleasing irony in an art critic writing about an art critic for whom, and for the artists around him, the most profound encounters with art seem to occur precisely when interpretation fails. While Eastham is tender in his descriptions of art, his acute observations of the people surrounding it can be lacerating. He has a formidable talent for summoning up a character – or skewering one – in a sentence. One woman possesses ‘the erotic hauteur of an academic who in her youth danced beneath filtered spotlights at psychedelic happenings’. Another, ‘a woman in those oversized metal-rimmed spectacles designed to signal to civilians that the wearer is an intellectual’. Eastham is exacting not only when it comes to how people appear, but also about the identities they are trying, sometimes desperately, to project. Despite the grieving anguish of its narrator, it is his wry, deadpan humour that carries the novel. There is a dryly comic sparring match with a ‘philanthropist’ who believes happiness can be quantified, and a conversation between partygoers about where, literally, ‘the shit is going’. At times it is not unlike a drawing-room comedy, with its sharp wit, back-and-forth banter and clever insults.
The metafictional frame allows the novel to avoid the aftermath of its most dramatic events, dwelling instead on the act of remembering and reconstructing them. I’m not convinced this framing adds to the reader’s understanding of the narrator’s grief or the events being recounted. The narrator returns to remarkably similar emotional terrain at the end: melancholic and still lost, but perhaps slightly more hopeful for the future. For all its suspicion of the contemporary artworld and its machinations, The Floating World remains surprisingly sincere about art itself. This is especially persuasive when Eastham uses art to give shape to experiences that elude explanation – love, pregnancy, grief – reminding us that beneath the bullshit posturing of the artworld is an unexpectedly earnest faith that art can make felt what we cannot quite articulate.
The Floating World by Ben Eastham. Fitzcarraldo Editions , £14.99 (softcover)

articles.title_orig: Why renewed Egypt-Ethiopia tensions are a problem for China
articles.title_zh: Why renewed Egypt-Ethiopia tensions are a problem for China
articles.content_orig:
You're reading an excerpt from Al-Monitor China-Middle East, where we analyze China's deepening engagement with the region. To get this newsletter in your inbox weekly, sign up here .
The renewed Egypt-Ethiopia escalation is a lose-lose proposition for China that threatens vital interests in both countries. As Cairo and Addis Ababa trade diplomatic expulsions, revive disputes over the Nile and over regional security and access to the Red Sea , Beijing faces mounting pressure to protect ties with two of its most important African partners.
From infrastructure and trade to security and diplomacy, China has deepened its web of interests in both Egypt and Ethiopia, emerging as the economic partner of choice in the Horn of Africa and within the wider Belt and Road network. While doing so, Beijing has tried to maintain a careful balance even as conflicts and bitter rivalries gripped that region.
The new round of escalation reached its peak last week as Ethiopia expelled an Egyptian diplomat, prompting Cairo to respond in kind by declaring an Ethiopian Embassy counselor persona non grata. The reciprocal moves came amid a broader regional escalation: Addis Ababa accused Egypt, Eritrea and Sudan last month of supporting a Tigray People’s Liberation Front-led opposition alliance, allegations all three countries deny.
Egypt then hosted a four-way summit with Eritrea, Sudan and Somalia on Oct. 4. The leaders stressed sovereignty and territorial integrity, said Red Sea security should remain primarily the responsibility of littoral states and rejected unilateral measures affecting the established water rights of downstream Nile countries.
The dispute has historically centered on two issues: access to the Red Sea and its management of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD). Cairo fears that unilateral operation of the dam, particularly during drought , could threaten water supplies in a country heavily dependent on the Nile. Ethiopia considers the project essential to electricity generation and economic development.
China’s critical ties with both
As Cairo and Addis Ababa trade accusations, Beijing is increasingly caught between a rock and a hard place. Egypt has only expanded ties with China in the last decade and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi has made eight official visits to China since taking office in 2014.
The economic relationship is substantial as Chinese companies expand their industrial presence in the Suez Canal Economic Zone while security and tech ties have only grown in the last decade. Egyptian officials said in September that 3,366 Chinese companies were operating in the country across sectors including textiles, solar energy, chemicals, automotive manufacturing and logistics. Bilateral trade reached $11.3 billion in the first half of 2026, up 21.5% from a year earlier. During President Xi Jinping’s September visit to Cairo, the two countries pledged to deepen cooperation in infrastructure, energy, manufacturing, artificial intelligence, renewable energy, electric vehicles and the digital economy.
Ethiopia is just as strategically important for China, and its recently reelected President Abiy Ahmed has visited Beijing four times since 2018. The two countries flaunted their “all-weather strategic partnership” in 2023 spanning infrastructure, transport, energy and trade.
Between 2010 and 2018, Chinese firms built the 752-kilometer Addis Ababa-Djibouti railway, the Addis Ababa-Adama Expressway and major industrial parks, bridges and telecommunications projects. Chinese state-owned enterprises dominate the shortlist for construction contracts on Ethiopia's new $12.5 billion Bishoftu International Airport project, according to Reuters.
China has traditionally avoided openly taking sides in the GERD dispute. But during Xi’s September visit to Egypt, Beijing moved closer to Cairo’s language.
In their joint statement, China recognized the Nile as Egypt’s “primary lifeline” and affirmed Egypt’s right to safeguard its water and food security. Both sides also called on Nile Basin states to respect international law and the principle of avoiding harm to other countries.
The statement did not name Ethiopia or directly oppose the GERD. Still, it supported principles Egypt has long invoked in calling for binding rules governing the dam’s operation.
China and Egypt also said Red Sea governance and security should primarily remain in the hands of littoral states — another sensitive issue for landlocked Ethiopia, which has increasingly pushed for reliable access to the sea.
For China, the risk goes beyond diplomacy.
Renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia could further destabilize Tigray and surrounding regions and potentially draw in neighboring states. China already experienced the commercial consequences of the previous Tigray conflict, when it evacuated hundreds of Chinese nationals in 2020 working on projects in the region.
More broadly, China’s Belt and Road strategy in the Horn depends on regional connectivity. Ethiopian industrial centers are linked to Djibouti’s ports through the Chinese-built Addis Ababa-Djibouti railway, connecting them to Red Sea shipping lanes and the Suez Canal.
A wider conflict could disrupt those supply chains, increase security and transport costs and make new investment riskier.
Cameron Hudson, a senior fellow in the Africa Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), the current situation limits Beijing’s options.
“China offers predictability in its engagement, but it looks for stability in return,” Hudson explained in an interview. “Feuds among its partners create a challenging operating environment.”
That leaves Beijing with a difficult balancing act: support regional stability, push for mediation and strengthen ties with Cairo without alienating Ethiopia.
But mediation isn’t China’s strong suit in the Horn, Hudson argued. “China’s diplomacy is not typically set up to mediate. Its strength is in managing a bilateral relationship, but has not traditionally excelled in managing competing interest across the region,” he said.
So what is realistic for China in mitigating the fallout? Hudson expects Beijing to take a wait-and-see approach.
“China might hit the pause button for the moment and re-engage when things have settled down. They typically let Washington do the heavy lifting,” he said. The problem, however, is that Washington is not actively mediating either .

articles.title_orig: World Mission Sunday has ‘borne fruit in my own life,’ says Pope Leo
articles.title_zh: World Mission Sunday has ‘borne fruit in my own life,’ says Pope Leo
articles.content_orig:
(OSV News) — The aim of World Mission Sunday (Oct. 18), established 100 years ago by Pope Pius XI, has “borne fruit in my own life,” said Pope Leo XIV.
The pope reflected on the annual observance in a video message posted by Vatican News to its YouTube channel Oct. 7. A transcript of the message was also published on the Vatican’s website.
In January, Pope Leo XIV announced he had chosen the theme “One in Christ, united in mission” for this year’s celebration, with his message for the day encouraging “the whole Church to continue its missionary journey with joy and zeal in the Holy Spirit.”
Established by Pope Pius XI in 1926 and universally observed by 1927, World Mission Sunday is a dedicated day of “prayer and missionary promotion throughout the Catholic world,” according to its founding decree.
Held on the next-to-last Sunday of October, the observance also includes a collection that serves as the primary financial support for the Pontifical Mission Societies, a worldwide network operating at the service of the pope and consisting of four organizations designated as pontifical by Pope Pius XI in 1922.
The Society for the Propagation of the Faith supports the evangelization efforts of the local church; the Missionary Childhood Association educates children about their part in the church’s missionary outreach; the Society of St. Peter the Apostle trains the next generation of missionary clergy and consecrated religious; and the Pontifical Missionary Union focuses on forming clergy, religious and pastoral leaders more deeply in their role as evangelizers.
In his video message, Pope Leo said, “Looking back on my youth, I can see how the prayers offered to the Lord of the harvest mysteriously helped prepare my heart to hear Jesus’ call to follow him as an Augustinian missionary.”
The future pope served for years in Peru, a country particularly blessed by missionary priests, said Father Anthony D. Andreassi, a priest of the Oratory of St. Philip Neri in Brooklyn, New York, and a researcher for the Pontifical Mission Societies USA.
In an Oct. 5 interview with OSV News, Father Andreassi explained how the 20th century saw an uptick in the number of North American priests, both diocesan and religious, assigned to Latin America, where the Church already had a 500-year presence, but “never enough of a native clergy.”
The Augustinian Order “started sending people into Peru in the 1960s,” said Father Andreassi. “And then, all of a sudden, you see Robert Prevost” — who would eventually become Pope Leo XIV — “there in the 1980s.”
In his video message, Pope Leo said “the prayers and contributions of the faithful encouraged and sustained my missionary work in Peru, as well as that of countless others throughout the world.”
“For this reason, I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to everyone who has supported World Mission Sunday over the years,” he added.
The pope said this year’s theme “invites us to reflect on the fundamental task of nurturing the Church’s unity in following Christ, particularly in our commitment and responsibility to spread the Gospel message of salvation to all people.”
Baptism makes each of the faithful “a member of the Body of Christ” with “a unique role in contributing to Jesus’ saving work.”
“Our Lord calls us to cooperate as one family, with the help of the Holy Spirit, to bring everyone everywhere into a communion of faith in Christ,” said Pope Leo.
He reaffirmed his appeal from his previously released message for the day, urging all to “commit to contributing to the great mission of evangelization — which is always a work of love — according to our own vocation and the gifts we have received.”
Prayers and “practical support” will be “a great help in bringing the Gospel of God’s love to everyone, especially the poorest and those most in need,” said the pope, quoting from his earlier message.
He thanked those who “carry on the legacy of World Mission Sunday” and “support generously the evangelizing mission of the Church throughout the world.”

articles.title_orig: Wildlife populations have declined 73% since 1970 – but many of the world’s animals still aren’t being counted
articles.title_zh: Wildlife populations have declined 73% since 1970 – but many of the world’s animals still aren’t being counted
articles.content_orig:
Wildlife populations around the world have declined by an average of 73% since 1970. That’s according to the WWF’s new 2026 Living Planet Index – a major estimate, updated every two years, of the changing state of nature. This does not mean that 73% of the world’s animals have disappeared. Rather, it is the average decline in the size of wildlife populations that is being monitored.
The index is one of the metrics used to track progress towards the UN’s biodiversity goals and shapes narratives of biodiversity loss across the world. But the data behind that 73% headline, one of the most comprehensive available, is still far from complete.
Very few, outside of those of us working at the coalface of handling biodiversity data, understand just how poorly wild animal populations are monitored. Though the world faces the joint crises of climate change and biodiversity loss, we can track climate change through thousands of weather stations or measures of atmospheric CO₂. Biodiversity is far harder to measure. Counting wildlife is highly resource intensive, generally can’t be done from space, and systematic monitoring is extremely patchy.
What this means is that, relative to the data we do possess, there are far, far more wildlife populations that no one is counting.
Though initiatives are seeking to address this, it will be years before they will produce outcomes. And we still have the issue of historic data gaps, that is, we cannot travel back in time to count populations of the past. This means the Living Planet Index and similar efforts to track how wildlife is changing must rely on whatever data is available. These come from ad hoc academic studies, patchy monitoring programmes, and management data for harvested species.
Some critiques of the index have focused on the fact that when these records are taken at face value, roughly the same number of populations are increasing as decreasing. Similar patterns are observed in one of the other biggest collections of population change data, BioTIME .
So why does the Living Planet Index show such a strong overall decline? One reason is that the populations we have data for are not necessarily representative of wildlife populations as a whole.
For example, the Living Planet Index is biased towards counts from protected areas, and preliminary analysis from our team indicates both it and BioTIME contain a disproportionate number of counts in areas of mostly undisturbed habitat – such as remote wilderness or national parks.
In other words, most of the information we possess about wildlife change worldwide could be from areas where we would hope biodiversity is doing okay. This might explain the balance of declining and increasing populations in the raw data. If we don’t account for this, we risk making major underestimates of how much biodiversity is declining.
Though there do tend to be “winners” from habitat loss or change, such as farmland birds that thrive after a forest is converted to agriculture, many instances of habitat loss result in far more populations declining than increasing, like conversions of tropical forest to monoculture plantations, or grasslands to towns or cities.
But the bias could also work in the other direction. The Living Planet Index might be more likely to have data on threatened species, or on species harvested by humans (such as fish). These are all species we might expect to be declining. The truth is, we don’t fully understand all the ways in which the wildlife counts we have could be biased, or how this could affect what we know.
The Living Planet Index takes steps to address bias by giving greater importance to counts from under-sampled regions such as Africa and South America.
There, the loss of undisturbed habitat is greater and there are far more species, so giving their population counts greater relative importance is a coarse way to balance some bias. It also includes data collected over very short periods – sometimes just two time points.
This sparseness comes with uncertainty about population trends, but excluding these populations would leave the index with even less data and make its underlying biases worse .
More sophisticated methods to understand bias in biodiversity science are in their infancy, and scientists are working hard to develop tools and make indicators more accurate. In the meantime, anyone interpreting the Living Planet Index must remember that the task presented to teams developing biodiversity indicators is twofold: not only to analyse existing data in rigorous ways but also to make adjustments so that the data itself is as representative as possible of the real world.
Getting this right is a phenomenally difficult task, especially for global indicators like the Living Planet Index, which have to produce a single narrative that summarises the great diversity of wildlife changes happening across the planet. As new methods emerge, scientists will work to ensure that the story told of global biodiversity loss is as accurate as possible.

articles.title_orig: Venezuela's Maduro, wife Flores charged in US over alleged torture
articles.title_zh: Venezuela's Maduro, wife Flores charged in US over alleged torture
articles.content_orig:
Ousted Venezuelan president and Cilia Flores have been in jail in New York since early January
Deposed Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, have been indicted for alleged conspiracy to commit torture, according to Manhattan federal court papers unsealed Thursday.
CNN first reported the expected indictment on Wednesday.
The superseding indictment was unsealed shortly before Flores appeared at court in her ongoing push for pre-trial release. Maduro and Flores have been held in a New York City jail since early January. They were captured in a US military operation and transported to New York to face “narcoterrorism” charges in a move that sparked widespread international outrage.
In the new charging document, the US attorneys office for the southern district of New York described how Maduro and his wife allegedly used horrific tactics to suppress opposition and maintain their control.
They presided “over a system of repression that relied on violence against political opposition, arbitrary detention, and the torture of detainees, including United States citizens”, the charging document said.
“That torture included electric shock, asphyxiation, rape, forced nudity, prolonged isolation, starvation, punishment cells, and psychological torture, such as threats to harm and kill victims’ families, including children,” it added.
Maduro and Flores, the new indictment alleged, “sat atop that violent power structure”.
Flores was integral to this effort, authorities claimed, saying she “helped develop this system of repression and ordered that individuals be tortured to protect her family members’ illegal activities”.
The victims of their torture included “US citizens “who were believed to pose a threat” to Maduro’s power.
“One particular United States citizen was detained in Venezuela and subjected to, among other things, deprivation of food and water, simulated drowning, repeated beatings, electric shock to his testicles, and forced injections.”
Both have pleaded not guilty in a criminal case first brought six years ago against them and numerous alleged co-conspirators. They face potential life prison sentences if convicted of being part of a conspiracy to send cocaine into the US.
Their attorneys have asked for the case to be dismissed on the grounds that they have immunity as the leader and first lady of a foreign country.
Lawyers for Flores, 69, have also argued that she has medical issues that cannot be treated effectively in jail, and that she could instead be allowed to live under 24-hour guard at a residence in New York.
They also said she suffered permanent scarring when she was “thrown against a wall or dresser” during the US military action that led to her capture.
Her lawyers said she had lost 25lbs (11kgs) while imprisoned at the Metropolitan detention center in Brooklyn and had been told that she might need heart surgery. They said she also suffered from “lingering lightheadedness, dizziness and shortness of breath” and might have suffered a minor heart attack in July.
Prosecutors opposed the bail request. In a court filing, they wrote that Flores would pose an “extreme risk of flight and danger to the public” if released. They also said she had been taken from the jail to get treatment at a local hospital, when care was needed.
Donald Trump’s administration has defended the raid to capture Maduro as a “surgical law enforcement operation”. Maduro has called himself a prisoner of war and his capture a kidnapping.
Flores is charged with participating in a cocaine importation conspiracy with Maduro, who served as Venezuela’s president from 2013 until his capture by US forces in January.
Lawyers for Flores said she was no threat to flee because she is “intent on supporting her husband with her constant presence”.
The Associated Press contributed to this report

Odyssey Launches Odyssey-3, Its Most Powerful Foundation World Model Built to Power AI Across the Physical World
New model demonstrates a shared understanding of the world across robots, humanoids, vehicles, drones, AI agents, and video games
Odyssey , an AI research company pioneering foundation world models, today announced Odyssey-3, its most powerful world model to date. The new model represents a significant advance toward general-purpose intelligence that can understand, predict, and interact with both physical and virtual environments.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261008756684/en/
Caption: Odyssey’s latest world model powering Flexion’s robot. Credit: Odyssey
World models learn from vast examples of the world evolving to predict and simulate what happens next, including how actions affect outcomes. Odyssey-3 gives intelligent systems a general understanding of how the world works before they are taught a specific task. The model has shown the ability to control robots and humanoids, drive vehicles, pilot drones, generate environments for training AI agents, and play video games. The new model has already been adopted by companies including Flexion, a leader in humanoid autonomy.
Trained on a vast dataset of visual observations of the world, Odyssey-3 builds on world models the company has been developing over the past three years. It has learned representations of physics, dynamics, cause and effect, and human behavior that can be applied across physical and virtual systems.
Using this pretrained foundation, Odyssey-3 enables physical agents: intelligent systems that can apply a shared understanding of the world across different machines, environments, and tasks. Rather than learning every new task entirely from scratch, these systems can draw on a broader model of how the world works and adapt that knowledge to new situations with relatively little additional experience.
“Odyssey-3 is a big step toward a single intelligence that can understand and operate in the world around us,” said Oliver Cameron, co-founder and CEO of Odyssey . “World models give physical agents a foundation of knowledge they can carry from one machine, environment, or task to another. We believe that the ability to learn broadly and then adapt with relatively little experience is the path toward increasingly general physical intelligence.”
The company has demonstrated Odyssey-3 across six domains:
Odyssey-3 is designed as a foundation that can span these domains rather than a model optimized for a single machine or application. By learning common representations of how environments behave and how actions change them, Odyssey is working toward world models that can transfer knowledge across increasingly diverse physical and virtual systems.
Odyssey is an AI lab pioneering general world models: causal, multimodal systems that learn to predict and interact with the world over long horizons. This foundational technology promises to revolutionize robotics, science, healthcare, education, gaming, defense, and beyond.
Odyssey’s founders previously pioneered one of the most complex applications of physical AI: self-driving cars. They’ve since brought together a world-class research team from DeepMind, Tesla, Waymo, Meta, Apple, and Wayve, whose members have contributed to language models, video models, world models and autonomous systems, including DeepMind Gemini, DeepMind Veo, Wayve GAIA and Tesla FSD.

articles.title_orig: USS Abraham Lincoln scheduled to dock in San Diego after harrowing stretch at sea
articles.title_zh: USS Abraham Lincoln scheduled to dock in San Diego after harrowing stretch at sea
articles.content_orig:
Deployment for nearly a year was marked by reports of supply shortages and deteriorating morale and mental health among crew
The USS Abraham Lincoln, the US aircraft carrier that has been deployed for nearly a year and has spent months supporting US military operations against Iran, is scheduled to dock in San Diego on Thursday afternoon.
It marks the end of a deployment that has been described as “one of the most operationally intense and consequential of the modern era” and that became marked by a record-setting stretch at sea, repeated deployment extensions, and reports of supply shortages and deteriorating morale and mental health among some crew members.
The Lincoln left San Diego last November, initially bound for the Pacific. But it was redirected to the Middle East after the US and Israel launched their war with Iran in late February. The carrier remained there until late August, when it was relieved by the USS George Washington and began its journey home .
Earlier in August, the Lincoln’s deployment made headlines and faced scrutiny as reports began surfacing about poor living conditions onboard the ship, including shortages of supplies and water, plumbing problems, low morale and worsening mental health among the roughly 5,000 personnel on the carrier. Two leading military newspapers also reported that there had been two attempts by sailors to jump overboard, causing concern among families and military health experts.
The reports prompted outrage from Democrats , while senior officials in the Trump administration pushed back . Pete Hegseth, the US defense secretary, called the reports “completely misrepresented ”, and when reporters asked Donald Trump if he thought the deployment had gone on too long, he responded : “Not nearly long enough” – a comment that angered some naval families.
In a statement at the time, Adm Brad Cooper, who heads US Central Command, claimed that of the US navy’s 11 active aircraft carriers, the Lincoln had “among the lowest number of cases related to mental health”. But he said that “this doesn’t mean that all is perfect”.
Cooper said that a long deployment at sea “is uniquely challenging and tough, and every single one of us, including me, reacts to stressors in different ways”.
Two weeks ago, as the Lincoln headed back to San Diego, Hung Cao, the acting navy secretary, acknowledged that eight service members from the Lincoln and its accompanying strike group attempted to take their own lives.
Sara Jacobs, a Democrat representing California’s 51st district who visited the Lincoln in late September, said in a statement last week that while she is “relieved that the USS Abraham Lincoln will soon be back in San Diego” and “looking forward to welcoming them home”, her “demand for accountability won’t end when they make port”.
“I will continue pushing for an [office of the inspector general] investigation into these conditions and a House armed services committee field hearing in San Diego to hear directly from these service members,” she said. “We need to prevent this crisis from happening ever again, and ultimately end the Iran war and bring all our service members home.”
On Wednesday, Hegseth visited the Lincoln ahead of its return, and praised the crew. He acknowledged that their deployment had not been “easy”.
“When you greet your families tomorrow, just pass my gratitude from the president and myself,” Hegseth said. “Let them know that their long wait, we believe, was in service of a righteous and historic mission.”
During his remarks, Hegseth announced that those onboard the vessel would be awarded the presidential unit citation, which, according to the US military , is conferred on units of the armed forces “for extraordinary heroism in action against an armed enemy”.
Ahead of the Lincoln’s arrival on Thursday afternoon, Blue Star Families, one of the largest US-based non-profit organizations supporting active military service members, veterans and their families, said in a statement that “every homecoming is an important moment for military families”.
The organization said that it “welcomes home the sailors of USS Abraham Lincoln and wants every family to know they’re not alone as they reconnect”.
In the weeks ahead, Blue Star Families said it will host appreciation days for Lincoln sailors and their families, including several events next month in San Diego.

articles.title_orig: Genre-defying Canadian poet Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
articles.title_zh: Genre-defying Canadian poet Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
articles.content_orig:
my mother said to me recently.
Why hold onto all that? And I said,
This quote is from the long, lyrical poem " The Glass Essay " published in Anne Carson's 1995 collection "Glass, Irony and God" — an entry point into the works of the 2026 Nobel Prize for Literature laureate .
In the poem, the narrator explores the burden of memory and obsessive desire after a failed love affair, all while regularly reflecting on Emily Brontë — an author renowned for her intense literary depiction of destructive and passionate love in " Wuthering Heights ."
The poem brings several of Carson's recurring obsessions together into one work. She has repeatedly written about desire, abandonment and jealousy, and has often used other literary figures as emotional doubles, as historical anchor points to her ideas.
In a way, "The Glass Essay" encapsulates Carson's method; the Canadian poet, essayist, translator and classicist has often intellectualized emotional themes by intertwining her personal reflections with analysis, etymology, translation, literary history and philosophical thought.
Another trademark of her work is the genre fludity found in "The Glass Essay," which — as the title indicates — is partly a literary criticism essay, even though it is also a poem due to its form.
"Almost all her literary production has centered upon the intersection between the philologist's obsession with words and the poet's desire for new meaning," noted Anders Olsson, chair of the Nobel Committee, in his description of the Nobel laureate on October 8.
Born in the Canadian city of Toronto, Carson first developed her fascination for ancient Greek myths as a teenager. She told literary journal The Brick that she spotted a bilingual edition of "Sappho" by Willis Barnstone in the display of a bookstore of a shopping mall in Ontario, and that had led her to ask a high school Latin teacher to teach her ancient Greek.
She went on to publish her doctoral thesis in Classics, entitled "Odi et Amo Ergo Sum " (I hate and I love, therefore I am).
Carson's first book of criticism, "Eros the Bittersweet," was published in 1986. It lays the foundation of her approach, as she draws on ancient Greek writers such as Sappho and Plato to examine how desire — and the obstacles between the lover and the beloved — creates emotional tension.
The book suggests that the ache of wanting is not separate from love; it is one of the things that makes  desire so powerful.
Because "Eros the Bittersweet" moves between Greek poetry, philosophy and literary criticism and personal interpretations, it is not considered a conventionally easy read. A more immediately engaging work and good starting point to discover Carson is the verse novel "Autobiography of Red," published in 1998.
"Autobiography of Red" was inspired by the ancient Greek myth of Heracles (or Hercules) and the red-winged monster Geryon, which the hero kills as his 10th task in his series of 12 monumental labors.
An otherwise minor figure from mythology, Geryon is turned into Heracles' lover in Carson's book. She reimagines the myth as a modern, queer coming-of-age story, with the monster experiencing love, jealousy, sexuality and heartbreak.
"We all feel we're monsters most of the time," explained Carson.
The work is accessible, funny and moving, and no deep knowledge of Greek mythology is required to enjoy it.
The key to reading Carson is not to expect every connection to be immediately clear. Her books reward curiosity rather than certainty, and her sprawling, non-linear web of knowledge can be compared to going down a hyperlinked rabbit hole of narrative ideas.
"Men in the Off Hours" (2000) is another intellectually playful collection of poems. Here Carson collides the modern with the ancient, with references to figures as diverse as Beethoven , Virginia Woolf, Emily Dickinson, Jean-Luc Godard, Sigmund Freud, Homer, Hokusai and Satan.
The poems bring together fragments of history, mythology and ordinary life, allowing unexpected emotional and intellectual connections to emerge.
In the spoken and sung performance piece "Norma Jeane Baker of Troy" (2019), Carson similarly brings together ancient and pop culture, reimagining the story of Helen of Troy alongside the life and cultural image of Marilyn Monroe .
How do people become the victims of desires they cannot control? This is a core theme Carson explores in "The Beauty of the Husband: A Fictional Essay in 29 Tangos," published in 2001.
It features the Canadian author's wry humor in a powerful and moving way, portraying erotic, painful and heartbreaking scenes from a doomed marriage: a 30-year obsession with a pathological liar whose singular redeeming quality is his sheer physical radiance.
The collection of poetry, which won her the T.S. Eliot Prize, is dedicated to John Keats, challenging the Romantic poet's famous aphorism, "Beauty is truth."

articles.title_orig: World Sight Day: Restoring sight where cataract surgery is scarce
articles.title_zh: World Sight Day: Restoring sight where cataract surgery is scarce
articles.content_orig:
Lloyd Williams, MD, PhD, discusses rising cataract blindness and low-cost surgery in conflict zones for World Sight Day.
Cataract remains a leading cause of vision impairment and blindness worldwide. At least 2.2 billion people have a near or distance vision impairment, and in at least 1 billion of those cases, the impairment could have been prevented or has yet to be addressed, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Cataract accounts for 94 million of those cases, and 1 in 2 people who need cataract surgery do not have access to it.¹
World Sight Day is an annual day of awareness held on the second Thursday of October and coordinated by the International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness (IAPB). This year, it falls on October 8. The 2026 #LoveYourEyes campaign centers on personal stories, lived experiences, and community action ahead of the first Global Summit for Eye Health on November 2 in Antigua and Barbuda.²
To mark the occasion, Lloyd Williams, MD, PhD , director of Duke Global Ophthalmology at Duke Eye Center in Durham, North Carolina, spoke with Ophthalmology Times about why cataract blindness continues to rise and how teams deliver high-quality surgery in low-resource settings. Williams received the American Academy of Ophthalmology's 2025 Outstanding Humanitarian Service Award for expanding access to cataract and corneal surgery in underserved regions.
Williams attributed the increase to aging populations in regions where ophthalmic care has not expanded, compounded by conflict and poverty that make many areas harder to reach. He cited a recent cataract camp in South Sudan.
"We literally had to negotiate a ceasefire in order to do cataract surgery," Williams told Ophthalmology Times .
Williams highlighted several organizations working to expand access to eye care. Readers can donate or get involved through the following: • Duke Global Ophthalmology: Give to Duke GO .³ • Cure Blindness Project: Donate ; ophthalmologists and practices can also join its Global Partners Program.⁴ • IAPB: Individuals can become a Love Your Eyes Visionary , and organizations can apply for membership .⁵ • CBM (Christian Blind Mission): Donate .⁶ • Sightsavers: Donate or fundraise through Sightsavers USA.⁷
On a recent trip to Abyei, surgery cost approximately $70 per case using manual small incision cataract surgery (MSICS), which requires a microscope as the only electrical equipment. In skilled hands, Williams said, MSICS achieves results roughly equivalent to those in the US. A $700,000 donation this year is expected to fund approximately 9000 surgeries, a volume he said would not be possible with phacoemulsification or laser-based approaches.
"I strongly believe that we're not providing somebody substandard care," Williams said.
Williams also addressed studies linking cataract surgery to lower rates of dementia diagnosis, which cannot yet establish cause and effect. He recalled veterans whose anxiety and depression appeared to improve after surgery during his residency, and he said he discusses the cognitive benefits of sight with families of older patients. Reflecting on his own vision problem as a resident, he described sight as "something that you could lose just like your arm."

articles.title_orig: Arizona congressional candidate says she was raped while repairing campaign sign
articles.title_zh: Arizona congressional candidate says she was raped while repairing campaign sign
articles.content_orig:
A congressional candidate in Arizona has said she was raped in a car park as she repaired campaign signs late at night in her district.
Bernadette Greene-Placentia, a Democrat, told the Phoenix New Times she was knocked unconscious during the alleged attack in the Phoenix suburb of Sun City on 14 August, waking up to find a man on top of her.
She said she did not initially notify police until filing a report with the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office two weeks later.
Her Republican opponent, Abraham Hamadeh, urged authorities in a statement to "investigate these serious allegations thoroughly, including finding all possible camera footage of the time and place".
"No American should become a victim of a crime in their own community," said Hamadeh, who is running for a second term in office.
Greene-Placentia told the Phoenix New Times she was "embarrassed" and "just wanted to forget", but felt compelled stand up for other victims.
The candidate said she often speaks on the campaign trail about fighting for Arizonans.
She told the Phoenix New Times: "I didn't feel like I could keep saying that if I weren't also fighting for women that are victims of sexual assault."
The BBC has contacted the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office for comment. A sheriff's spokesman told the New York Times the investigation was ongoing.
After the attack, Greene-Placentia said she withdrew from the public for two days, staying in an apartment separate from her husband and skipping a campaign event.
When she emerged, her husband, campaign staff and others in her circle noticed she was acting differently, according to Phoenix New Times.
Greene-Placentia said she did not see a doctor following the alleged attack in congressional district eight and did not receive a sexual assault examination.
She said her memory of what happened was spotty and she did not get a good look at either of the two assailants, but described them as white men, according to the New York Times.
She told the Phoenix New Times that one assailant may have made a comment about her political affiliation, together with a misogynistic slur, although she could not be certain.
The candidate said she was concerned voters might think it was a political stunt to win points in a heavily Republican district. She also expressed concern that the allegations might overshadow her messaging around affordability.

Isaias is a Category 1 hurricane with sustained winds of 85 mph, according to the National Hurricane Center’s 10 a.m. CT update. That’s an increase of 5 mph from just three hours ago and shows that the hurricane is starting to bulk up again.
Isaias continues to battle some storm-disrupting winds in the atmosphere and dry air that led to its brief strength plateau earlier this morning. But it’s still forecast to reach Category 2 strength this evening and peak as a high-end Category 2 with 110 mph winds overnight Thursday or Friday morning.
Mandatory evacuation orders have been issued for parts of Gulf and Okaloosa counties on the northwest Florida coastline. Walton County has issued a voluntary evacuation notice for low-lying areas.
Governor Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency for 25 counties across the state on Tuesday. Pensacola Mayor D.C. Reeves also issued an emergency declaration for city.
Multiple counties are closing their offices beginning either Thursday or Friday, including Escambia , Okaloosa , Washington and Calhoun counties.
The sun has come up to reveal Hurricane Isaias and its swirling clouds above the Gulf’s record-warm water.
True color satellite imagery shows us what a storm looks like with the naked eye from space — think of it as what you’d see if you were on the space station.
But you need sunlight to illuminate the clouds and use this imagery. The storm’s bright white clouds appear in the loop as the satellite captures the moment of this morning’s sunrise.
Here’s a look at Isaias’ impacts and when to expect them in cities along the Gulf Coast.
For those who lived through Helene, another hurricane bringing rain to the mountains may stir understandable anxiety. But Isaias’ forecast points to a more limited flood threat.
Parts of the southern Appalachians could see 3 to 5 inches Saturday, with locally significant flooding possible.
During Helene, some mountain areas received up to 10 inches before the hurricane arrived. Moisture streaming ahead of Helene fueled a separate area of persistent downpours, known as a “predecessor rain event,” or PRE.
The hurricane then dumped torrential rain onto saturated ground, with mountain slopes enhancing the rainfall. The combined multiday event piled up 20 to 30 inches of rain in some parts of western North Carolina.
Isaias’ quick movement should help limit rainfall totals, though locally higher amounts remain possible. Residents should keep watching for forecast changes as the storm draws closer.
Isaias is forecast to run into some storm-disrupting wind shear the closer it gets to the US coast. This shear — changes in wind speed or direction at different levels of the atmosphere — is going to push Isaias a little off-kilter, focusing the worst of its wind and rain on the north side of the storm.
This lopsidedness will weaken Isaias — but also expand the reach of its winds.
A stronger storm tends to stay compact, like an ice skater spinning. Try to knock that same skater off balance, they’ll put out their arms to steady themself.
That’s basically the same thing we’re expecting with Isaias’ winds — instead of staying confined closer to the center, they’ll stretch out farther. More places could be hit with Isaias’ strong winds as a result, even if the storm is a bit weaker overall.
If Isaias makes landfall as a hurricane, it will mark the first hurricane landfall anywhere in the United States in two years.
No hurricane has come ashore in the US since 2024’s Hurricane Milton . Milton slammed into Florida’s Gulf Coast as a Category 3 major hurricane on October 9, 2024.
Isaias is forecast to weaken, but still remain a formidable storm before landfall Friday night or very early Saturday morning. It could come ashore as a Category 1 or a lower-end Category 2 hurricane before quickly becoming a tropical storm after landfall.
Regardless of its strength, Isaias will be the fourth named storm to make landfall in the US this season. The three others have been short-lived tropical storms: Arthur impacted Texas on June 17; Bertha hit Louisiana on July 22; and Edouard made landfall near the Texas-Louisiana border on September 1.
All Mobile County and Baldwin County Public schools in Alabama will be closed on Friday as Hurricane Isaias is expected to impact the northern Gulf Coast this weekend.
“We do not like to do this, because it affects so many, but we have to take all factors into consideration and of course, the most important, the safety of our students and our staff,” Baldwin County Public Schools Superintendent Marty McRae said announcing the closure on Wednesday .
All of Baldwin County Public Schools’ afterschool and extracurricular activities scheduled for Friday and Saturday are also canceled.
“I cannot risk anyone’s safety,” Mobile County Public Schools Superintendent Chresal Threadgill said in his closure announcement . “The weather conditions currently remain extremely unpredictable.”
Isaias remains a Category 1 hurricane with sustained winds of 80 mph, according to the National Hurricane Center’s 7 a.m. CT update.
The hurricane has maintained its strength over the past few hours but is still set to strengthen today. It’s forecast to peak as a high-end Category 2 hurricane sometime Thursday night.
A Hurricane Hunter aircraft is currently flying into Isaias, so we’ll get a more precise measurement of its current strength soon.
At least 14 Florida Panhandle counties are closing public schools Friday, and many have closed Thursday, according to the state’s Department of Education.
Florida State University’s campus in Panama City is also closed.
The right side of a hurricane, relative to its forward motion, typically packs the most extreme conditions, and it’s all because of their counterclockwise rotation.
Wind speeds are amplified because the rotation pushes air in the same direction as the storm is moving. The area with the most extreme winds and intense storms sits just to the right of a hurricane’s eye, in the eye wall.
Because of boosted winds, tornadoes also occur more frequently on the right side. Faster winds increase areas of wind shear — a change in wind speed or direction with height — which tornadoes need to spin up.
Similarly, surge is also enhanced. As storms approach land, wind piles up and pushes seawater towards the coast on the right side of a hurricane. On the left side of a hurricane, wind does the opposite and can actually drain bays.
This will all be true for Isaias but may be even more so because it’s expected to become lopsided as it battles wind shear near the Gulf Coast. More thunderstorms and rain will likely be concentrated on the hurricane’s eastern half.
Isaias is guaranteed to knock out power and down trees where it makes landfall along the coast, but outages could extend further inland into parts of the Southeast.
Isaias will be moving fast and grow larger before it moves inland. Those are two of the factors that will fuel wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph that will spread northward into parts of central and northern Alabama, northern Georgia and northeast Mississippi on Saturday.
Those gusts are nowhere near as fierce as what the coast will see, but it could be enough to cause at least isolated to scattered power outages, particularly in Alabama.
As Tropical Storm Isaias heads towards the Gulf Coast, many residents began preparing days in advance.
Residents flocked to grocery stores and gas stations in Pensacola, Florida to stock up in preparation causing long lines at some locations.
As Hurricane Isaias approaches the Gulf Coast, all eyes are on how it will impact one of the biggest games of the college football season.
The storm could make landfall Saturday, hours before No. 2 Georgia plays No. 6 Alabama in Tuscaloosa in a game that President Donald Trump is planning to attend.

A webinar on 16 October will commemorate World Food Day and say farewell to the UN special rapporteur for the Right to Water and Sanitation.
The webinar will take the World Food Day theme “ Innovate today. Nourish tomorrow.” The discussion will explore what innovation can look like when we place food security, water, land, human rights, and ecological sustainability at the centre.
World Food Day is observed on 16 October each year and provides an opportunity to draw attention to hunger and food insecurity while strengthening collective action towards food systems that are sustainable, equitable, and resilient. This year ’ s webinar will bring together United Nations mandate holders, faith-based organisations, civil society organisations, and community practitioners to explore some of the challenges shaping food insecurity today – including poverty, unsustainable agricultural practices and climate change – and to share approaches that are contributing to resilience, food sovereignty, and sustainable livelihoods.
The session will also provide an opportunity to hear from Prof. Pedro Arrojo-Agudo, UN special rapporteur on the human right to safe drinking water and sanitation, whose six-year mandate concludes in November 2026.

NORTHBROOK, Ill. and WEATHERFORD, Texas, Oct. 8, 2026
Thermal Charge® Heat Transfer Fluids and AI-Powered Monitoring Unite to Deliver Predictive Cooling-Loop Health Management
NORTHBROOK, Ill. and WEATHERFORD, Texas , Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Old World Industries (OWI), a leading manufacturer of coolant and heat transfer solutions best known for its brands of PEAK® and Thermal Charge® Heat Transfer Fluids, and Integrity Systems, a critical infrastructure monitoring company, today announced a strategic partnership to combine coolant expertise with real-time monitoring, predictive analytics and intelligent diagnostics for data center cooling systems.
As AI and other high-density computing workloads place increasing demands on data center infrastructure, operators need greater visibility into the real-time health and performance of their cooling systems. Any downtime or disruptions to the system can have significant operational and financial consequences, making proactive monitoring and maintenance critical for data center operators. Periodic laboratory testing provides important point-in-time information about coolant condition; the OWI-Integrity Systems partnership is designed to complement that testing with continuous field monitoring that can alert operators of changing cooling-loop conditions between testing intervals.
"Unscheduled downtime remains one of the most expensive risks facing data center operators today," said Greg Noethlich, Chief Executive Officer of OWI. "This partnership helps customers move from reactive problem-solving to predictive maintenance, helping avoid the substantial costs associated with unexpected system failures."
Integrity Systems' real-time industrial monitoring, predictive analytics and intelligent diagnostics capabilities are designed to work alongside existing controls and monitoring systems. Its platform brings together sensor data, operating context, maintenance history and operator knowledge to help identify developing problems and guide maintenance decisions.
"We founded Integrity Systems to close the gap between what industrial operators need and what predictive monitoring actually delivers," said Brett Wade, Chief Executive Officer of Integrity Systems. "By combining continuous field monitoring with OWI's coolant expertise, the partnership delivers ongoing visibility into coolant performance, helping operators make informed maintenance decisions based on real-time operating conditions."
The collaboration also creates an opportunity to generate additional real-world operating data on coolant performance. Those insights can help inform future product validation and development while giving operators greater context about cooling system conditions in live environments.
"We see AI's future being shaped not only by the size of the data centers behind it, but by the ability to deploy increasing levels of intelligence at the edge," said Connor Wooley, Chief Technology Officer of Integrity Systems. "Our goal is to lead in that space by delivering AI where work is performed and critical decisions are made. Our agentic harness is designed to turn deep analysis and verified operating experience into specialized AI that runs locally. With OWI, we're applying that approach to coolant and cooling-system health, helping operators understand what is changing, why it matters, and when to act. But our vision extends further, an operating system for intelligent infrastructure that can carry that capability beyond continuous human reach, from remote industrial environments to space. The goal is intelligence that can operate where people cannot always be, without depending on a distant data center for every decision."
Together, OWI and Integrity Systems are enabling a new standard for cooling-system assurance that helps data center operators improve uptime, protect critical infrastructure and confidently scale for growing computing demands. To learn more about the partnership, visit thermalcharge.com or integrityus.ai.

articles.title_orig: New GETI publication explores future of Christian unity
articles.title_zh: New GETI publication explores future of Christian unity
articles.content_orig:
A new publication from the World Council of Churches (WCC) Commission on Ecumenical Education and Formation (EEF) brings together the voices and theological reflections of young ecumenists from around the world who attended the 2025 edition of the WCC Global Ecumenical Theological Institute (GETI). It brings fresh inputs to the pressing question for the churches today: Where now for visible unity?
From left: Rev. Prof. Dr Meehyun Chung, moderator of the WCC Commission on Ecumenical Education and Formation; Prof. Dr Ani Ghazaryan Drissi, WCC programme executive for Ecumenical Theological Education and coordinator of GETI 2025; Rev. Dr Nathan Digby, GETI 2025 facilitator and member of the WCC Commission on Ecumenical Education and Formation; during the launch event of the GETI 2025 book on 8 October.
“ GETI 2025: Voices and Visions of Transformative Unity,” edited by Prof. Dr Ani Ghazaryan Drissi and Rev. Prof. Teddy Chalwe Sakupapa, emerges from the WCC ’ s 4th GETI, held in the context of the Sixth World Conference on Faith and Order in Wadi El Natrun, Egypt. The publication, launched on 8 October, during the biannual meeting of the EEF Commission, comes at a significant moment.
“ The fruits of ecumenical dialogue must take root in the lives of our churches,” said Ghazaryan. “ The GETI 2025 message brought this bold challenge to the Sixth World Conference on Faith and Order and the wider ecumenical movement: let the unity we confess become the life we share.”
This publication carries that call forward, she added, through voices and visions rooted in different churches, cultures, and lived realities. “ Their theological reflections invite us to ask how the fruits of ecumenical dialogue can shape our communities, deepen our relationships, and renew our common witness,” said Ghazaryan. “ They call us to listen more deeply, confront exclusion, and share responsibility for the future of our churches.”
Bossey students who took part of GETI 2025 shared their testimonies during the launch event.
The volume presents a global and contextually grounded exploration of Christian unity. Its contributors reflect on reception, Nicaea, pilgrimage, trust and companionship, while also addressing colonial wounds, trauma, migration, ethnic violence, Palestine, digital ecumenism, and ecological crisis.
Rather than treating unity as an abstract theological ideal, the book emphasizes unity as something that must be embodied through relationships, truth-telling, healing, solidarity, and public witness. Its concluding message describes young ecumenists as contributors to the present and future of the ecumenical movement.
GETI 2025 facilitator and EEF commissioner Rev. Dr Nathan Digby explained that a central goal of the WCC ’ s Ecumenical Theological Education work is to provide opportunities for emerging ecumenical leaders to be formed in ecumenism and to ensure that their voices are heard, encouraged, and shared with the wider church.
“ The publication of GETI 2025: Voices and Visions for Transformative Unity gives concrete expression to this commitment,” he said. “ As part of their theological formation, students participating in GETI 2025 developed academic papers exploring the theme of visible Christian unity in relation to their own theological interests, contexts, and experiences.”
This volume recognizes and celebrates their intellectual and theological work while creating a platform through which their perspectives can contribute to broader conversations about the future of Christian unity, added Digby.
“ By bringing these emerging voices together in one publication, GETI 2025: Voices and Visions for Transformative Unity not only documents an important dimension of the GETI experience but also invests in the next generation of ecumenical thinkers and leaders, whose insights and visions are essential for shaping a more transformative and visible unity among Christians.”
Published by WCC Publications, the book offers churches, theological institutions, students, and ecumenical partners a rich resource for reflection and conversation on the future of Christian unity.
The session also included the presentation of the GETI Visual Report and a short video featuring voices and moments of GETI 2025.
The EEF Commission is meeting at the WCC Ecumenical Institute at Bossey 4-9 October.

articles.title_orig: Police accept Andrew search warrants were unlawful, court hears
articles.title_zh: Police accept Andrew search warrants were unlawful, court hears
articles.content_orig:
Thames Valley Police has accepted that the search warrants it used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes earlier this year were unlawful, the High Court has heard.
The force said it accepted that the "initial court's decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect" before they searched the former prince's properties on 19 February.
Andrew was arrested by Thames Valley Police on suspicion of misconduct in public. He denies any wrongdoing.
The criminal investigation is ongoing and the items seized in the raids on his homes in Norfolk and Berkshire will remain in police custody while his legal challenge over this material continues.
Andrew's lawyers have used a judicial review to challenge the actions of the force's chief constable and the Central Criminal Court.
His arrest in February arose after the US Department of Justice published documents which suggested he had forwarded confidential information to the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein when Mountbatten-Windsor was a UK trade envoy in 2010.
He has consistently denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein.
The court heard on Thursday that Thames Valley Police took possession of documents and electronic devices when they raided Andrew's homes.
Thames Valley Police's position was that they had applied for search warrants under section eight and section nine of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 at a hearing at the Central Criminal Court the day before the search.
That court determined that only section eight search warrants were needed and they were granted on that basis - but subsequently, a legal challenge established that the court should have issued them under the section nine.
The conditions for the warrants were that there had to be reasonable grounds for believing that any documents used for business or in a paid or unpaid role in which an undertaking of confidence had been given should not be seized.
Thames Valley Police now admits the judge who granted the warrants could not have been sure of this.
A Thames Valley Police spokesperson said: "The agreement that led to the quashing of the warrants relates specifically to a decision made by the court regarding the legal basis for these and is not a judgement on our ongoing investigation.
"We ensured the court was presented with all the necessary information and paperwork to inform their decision, following the correct legal processes throughout.
"We accept the position that the initial court's decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect and therefore these must be legally quashed.
"Legal proceedings are currently ongoing to decide how material seized during the searches will be managed and whether we can lawfully retain it in support of our ongoing investigation."
The force said its "investigation into alleged misconduct in public office by a man in his 60s from Norfolk remains ongoing, and we continue to pursue all reasonable lines of enquiry to effectively and fairly progress this investigation".
